subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should sandbox Docker image builds adopt only APT retries, or also intentionally accept `--fix-missing` partial-install semantics?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` directly addresses transient fetch failures, while `--fix-missing` changes install failure behavior for required sandbox tools and needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Retry-only Dockerfile change
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5`, remove `--fix-missing`, and require inspectable build plus package-presence proof for the linked PR or a replacement.

options.title: Accept `--fix-missing` intentionally
options.body: Keep the flag only if maintainers want partial-install semantics and add package verification or documented recovery for incomplete images.

options.title: Close the linked PR and defer
options.body: If the behavior is not worth changing now, leave current fail-closed Dockerfiles as-is and close the implementation candidate.

recommendation.title: Retry-only Dockerfile change
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5`, remove `--fix-missing`, and require inspectable build plus package-presence proof for the linked PR or a replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main and Docker cache/release history makes this the closest evidence-backed routing candidate for the Dockerfile setup behavior.
